hypothesis: Duplicated inlined multibyte validation inflates print_utf8. One shared out-of-line multibyte decoder may reduce caller code footprint enough to outweigh a call on each multibyte attempt. This is unverified; no causal bottleneck share is assumed.
intervention: Only extract the unchanged multibyte body from utf8_at into #[inline(never)] utf8_multibyte_at(bytes, at, lead). ASCII inline return and all validation predicates, checked scalar conversion, widths, row loop and parser remain unchanged.
build: Fresh serial exact release test builds via build-engine-arm.py. Control byte-matches retained i28 control. Restore source bytes in finally. Selected terminal untouched.
correctness: Both arms: existing release terminal tests (383 passed, 11 ignored), exhaustive decoder and guarded-tail tests included; 64x200 differential streams before timing.

engine.primary: Unicode median paired CPU-rate ratio >=1.02, wins>losses, six-workload Holm p<.05, and all six median CPU ratios >=.98. Point guards are not noninferiority proof.
engine.stop: Exactly 12 pairs; no pilot, exclusions, reruns, rescue variants, pooling, threshold changes or optional stopping. Reject if screen fails. If it clears, separate fresh prospective PTY/Ghostty gates required before promotion.

mechanism: Exact timing ELF static census of print_utf8, Engine::apply and new multibyte helper. Caller bytes and call edges describe codegen, not dynamic causal cost.
limits: Sequential shared-host best-of-five engine sessions, not independent inner samples, real-terminal/Ghostty ranking or world-championship acceptance. Calls and code/data layout change together.
